q: When is the Island ferry busiest?

queries.purpose: Average riders per day by month (complete years 2016-2025)
queries.sql: SELECT strftime(d, '%b') AS label, round(avg(day_total)) AS value FROM (SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) AS d, sum(tickets_redeemed) AS day_total FROM ferry WHERE year(ts) BETWEEN 2016 AND 2025 GROUP BY 1) GROUP BY month(d), strftime(d, '%b') ORDER BY month(d)

queries.purpose: Average riders per day by day of week (summer, Jun-Aug, 2016-2025)
queries.sql: SELECT strftime(d, '%a') AS label, round(avg(day_total)) AS value FROM (SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) AS d, sum(tickets_redeemed) AS day_total FROM ferry WHERE year(ts) BETWEEN 2016 AND 2025 AND month(ts) IN (6,7,8) GROUP BY 1) GROUP BY isodow(d), strftime(d, '%a') ORDER BY isodow(d)

queries.purpose: Average riders per hour of day (summer, Jun-Aug, 2016-2025)
queries.sql: SELECT lpad(CAST(h AS VARCHAR), 2, '0') || ':00' AS label, round(sum(tickets_redeemed) * 1.0 / count(DISTINCT d)) AS value FROM (SELECT hour(ts) AS h, date_trunc('day', ts) AS d, tickets_redeemed FROM ferry WHERE year(ts) BETWEEN 2016 AND 2025 AND month(ts) IN (6,7,8)) GROUP BY h ORDER BY h

story.lead: Summer Saturdays around noon are busiest.
story.sub: Island ferry tickets redeemed, complete years 2016-2025, in 15-minute counts added up by day and hour.

points.p: Riders per day climb from spring to a peak in August, then fall quickly.
points.more: August averages 9,768 riders a day and July 8,699. January is the quietest at 492 a day.

points.h: Weekends are far busier than weekdays
points.p: In summer, Saturday and Sunday carry about double the weekday crowds.
points.more: Saturday averages 12,513 riders and Sunday 11,518. Tuesday is the lowest at 5,521, and Friday is the busiest weekday at 7,257.

points.p: On summer days, ridership builds through the morning and peaks around noon.
points.more: The 12:00 hour averages 995 riders, with 11:00 close at 986. By 18:00 it falls to 341, and before 08:00 it is under 60 an hour.

q: Which subway stations have the most delays?

queries.purpose: Stations with the most delays (incidents with delay minutes above 0)
queries.sql: SELECT station AS label, count(*) AS value FROM subway_delays WHERE min_delay > 0 AND station IS NOT NULL GROUP BY station ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 15

queries.purpose: Stations with the most total delay minutes
queries.sql: SELECT station AS label, sum(min_delay) AS value FROM subway_delays WHERE min_delay > 0 AND station IS NOT NULL GROUP BY station ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 15

queries.purpose: Stations with the longest average delay (stations with at least 30 delays)
queries.sql: SELECT station AS label, round(avg(min_delay), 1) AS value FROM subway_delays WHERE min_delay > 0 AND station IS NOT NULL GROUP BY station HAVING count(*) >= 30 ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 15

story.lead: Kipling station has the most delays.
story.sub: TTC subway delay incidents with delay minutes above 0, January 2025 to August 2026.

stat.caption: delays at Kipling station, the most of any station

points.h: Kipling, Kennedy and Wilson lead on delay count
points.p: Kipling station had the most delays, followed closely by Kennedy and Wilson.
points.more: Kipling had 578 delays, Kennedy (Line 2) 537, Wilson 513 and Bloor 504. Finch had 464 and Eglinton 446.

points.h: Eglinton loses the most minutes overall
points.p: Eglinton station tops the list for total minutes of delay.
points.more: Eglinton added up to 4,001 minutes, ahead of Kipling at 3,461 and Kennedy at 3,136. Victoria Park and Sheppard West each passed 3,000 minutes despite fewer delays.

points.h: Woodbine has the longest typical delay
points.p: Among stations with at least 30 delays, Woodbine delays last longest on average.
points.more: Woodbine averaged 12.3 minutes per delay, then Sheppard West at 12 and Islington at 11.9. Eglinton averaged 9 minutes.

q: What are the most popular dog names?

queries.purpose: Top 15 dog names in 2025 by licensed dogs
queries.sql: SELECT upper(left(name, 1)) || lower(substr(name, 2)) AS label, licensed_count AS value FROM pet_names WHERE animal = 'DOG' AND year = 2025 ORDER BY licensed_count DESC LIMIT 15

queries.purpose: Top 15 dog names, average licensed dogs per year 2020-2025
queries.sql: SELECT upper(left(name, 1)) || lower(substr(name, 2)) AS label, round(avg(licensed_count)) AS value FROM pet_names WHERE animal = 'DOG' AND year BETWEEN 2020 AND 2025 GROUP BY name ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 15

queries.purpose: How the most popular name has changed year by year
queries.sql: SELECT CAST(year AS VARCHAR) AS label, licensed_count AS value FROM pet_names WHERE animal = 'DOG' AND year BETWEEN 2020 AND 2025 AND name = (SELECT name FROM pet_names WHERE animal = 'DOG' AND year BETWEEN 2020 AND 2025 GROUP BY name ORDER BY sum(licensed_count) DESC LIMIT 1) ORDER BY year

story.lead: Luna and Charlie are Toronto's top dog names.
story.sub: Licensed dogs in Toronto, 2020 to 2025 (top 200 names per year only).

stat.caption: licensed dogs named Luna in 2025, the most of any name

points.p: Luna was the most common name among licensed dogs in 2025, ahead of Charlie.
points.more: Luna had 549 dogs and Charlie 491. Bella was third with 386, then Coco with 342 and Milo with 315.

points.h: Charlie leads over the six years
points.p: Averaged over 2020 to 2025, Charlie comes first and Luna second.
points.more: Charlie averaged 529 dogs a year and Luna 493. Bella was third at 405. Max, Coco and Daisy followed.

points.p: The top name over the six years, Charlie, peaked in 2021 and has been lower since.
points.more: Charlie went from 595 dogs in 2021 to 491 in 2025. It was 553 in 2020 and 488 in 2024.
